The deck's home is the three-torus: every clock wraps, and no flat frame can draw all eighty-one moves without lying. Here the body the study found is inhabited. The shuttle is the standing cell, derived from the clock and never drawn; the thread is its walk, cooling toward the past; a step of flow against turn crosses the seam, and the wall of the next room glimmers into being to receive it; a carry passes home through the null. THE LOOM, READ

THE BODYThe study's own object at full scale: each card's knot wound p against q on its golden torus, in its metal, links weaving their counter's, every crossing sorted honestly in depth. The fifty-four inner roads run beneath; the Seed is dark at the heart, the null never lit.
THE WALLS, AS WEATHERThe neighbouring rooms are not furniture; they are weather. A wall stays invisible until the thread actually crosses the seam, then the receiving wall of the next room glimmers into being, takes the thread, and cools away with it. There is no edge of the world on a torus; there is only the world again, shown exactly when the walk uses it.
THE SHUTTLEThe standing cell, the canon's own seating of the moment: the orbit on time, the moon on depth, the spin on state. Derived from the clock, never drawn; it wears the breathing ring, and it says where the moment stands, never what to do with it.
THE THREAD, AND THE CLOTHThe shuttle's walk, cooling toward the past and grown only forward: the loom does not unweave. An hour's step walks one road; a seam step leaves the room and returns from the other side; a carry passes home through the null, the thread's one lawful visit to the Seed. And beneath the living thread lies the cloth: roads the walk has repeated this sitting grow worn and bright, recurrence shown as geometry. A fresh NOW is a fresh bolt, and nothing is ever kept or sent.
THE ROSETTE, WORNThe loom's default face: the study's finest dress with time moving in it. The octahedron of faces, the cuboctahedron of edges, the cube of corners, each on its own sphere, the thread weaving straight through the shells because the dress never moved a seat, and the shell the shuttle stands on breathing with the hour, the restlessness as a tide. The still centre never breathes: the null is never lit. The button bares the body instead.
THE CRANKOne flow, every wheel at its true ratio. Slowed, the shuttle walks road by road; quickened, the days pour and the thread shows the walk's weather. The loom weaves unwatched, on the astrolabe's own lesson.
